summary: Tested the new Subscriptions/Payments feature (Featured + VIP plans, Stripe checkout, subscription gate on /api/providers, VIP-first sort, dashboard banner, /subscribe page, /payment-success polling). Backend: 15/15 pytest cases pass (PLANS allowlist, server-side validation, server-computed amount, payment_transactions row, gate, VIP sort, detail flags, ownership 403, 404). Frontend: VIP pill on Sophia (first card), client→/subscribe redirect to /dashboard, Sophia dashboard 'VIP Featured · live' banner with 30 days remaining + Renew CTA, /subscribe totals (€55 default → €30 → €55 after vip_4w add) all working. Pay button correctly redirects to checkout.stripe.com with cs_test_ session. ONE deviation from spec: /payment-success short-circuits to 'failed' card on first poll when Stripe returns payment_status='unpaid', so it never reaches MAX_ATTEMPTS=8 nor shows the 'Still processing' timeout card — contradicts the explicit testing requirement.

ui_bugs.issue: Polling short-circuits to state='failed' on FIRST response when data.payment_status === 'unpaid'. Spec requires polling every ~2s up to MAX_ATTEMPTS=8 (~16s) for an unpaid open session, then showing the 'Still processing' (state='timeout') card. As implemented, only 1-2 calls fire and the user sees 'Payment didn't complete' / Try again card instead. This is a functional deviation from the review request requirement.

action_items: Decide intended behaviour for /payment-success when Stripe reports payment_status='unpaid'. To match the review-request spec, remove the `data.payment_status === 'unpaid'` short-circuit in PaymentSuccess.js line 33 (keep only `data.status === 'expired'` as the failed-state trigger) so polling continues for ~16s before falling into the 'Still processing' timeout state. Alternatively, update the spec to accept the current 'fail-fast on unpaid' UX.
critical_code_review_comments: PaymentSuccess.js: short-circuiting on `payment_status === 'unpaid'` defeats the polling pattern; in real Stripe flow the redirect lands before webhook processes, so a brief 'pending → paid' transition is normal and polling exists for that window. As written, the user will see a red X 'Payment didn't complete' card the moment they land — confusing.
server.py _activate_subscription_for_session is correctly idempotent (status==complete short-circuit, payment_status==paid required) — good.
server.py /api/providers gate uses `featured_until > now` with naive UTC consistently with Mongo storage — good. The VIP sort sorts non-VIP secondarily by created_at desc which is sensible.
Subscribe.js: useMemo total uses `(o)=>o.id===vipPlan)?.price || 0`; good. Origin URL is sent from window.location.origin (correct).
server.py CheckoutBody has no length / format validation for origin_url — minor, server doesn't trust it for amount calc, only for redirect URLs.
server.py PLANS dict is the single source of truth for amount (good — server-side allowlist enforced).

rca of the issue: PaymentSuccess.js useEffect (lines 25-46) calls `poll()` once. Inside, line 33 treats `data.payment_status === 'unpaid'` as terminal failure and sets state='failed', returning before scheduling another setTimeout. The backend /api/subscriptions/status/{sid} returns payment_status='unpaid' for any open Stripe checkout session that has not yet been paid (Stripe's normal initial state). Consequence: the polling never iterates, attempts never reach MAX_ATTEMPTS=8, and the timeout 'Still processing' branch is unreachable in the standard 'just landed, payment not yet captured' flow. Mitigation: move 'unpaid' out of the failed-state trigger, leaving only `data.status === 'expired'` as terminal failure (an expired Stripe session truly cannot be paid).
